findings.claim: cmd/consensus/main.go never starts the async ToolExecutor: harness.NewToolExecutor has zero production callers (only internal/harness tests). tool_requests rows would sit pending forever in a stock serve.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'NewToolExecutor' --include='*.go' → only tool_executor.go (def) + tool_executor_test.go; serve log shows 'harness: heartbeat loop started' and no tool_executor start line.

findings.claim: Agent-issued tool requests from the LIVE interactive path never reach tool_requests: planning.ActionToolCall persists them to staging_buffer (cmd_type=tool_call_ref) and suspends the session in tool_exec, but nothing in-product drains tool_call_ref → tool_requests and nothing re-wakes the session with the result. Only the H3 shim implements the hand-off (stagedToolRequests/recordToolResultIntoStaging/FeedToolResult) for its own external clients. A goal session that requests a tool hangs in tool_exec until an external executor intervenes (session had to be re-woken manually; done via the shim's documented convention).
findings.evidence: runB server.log: 'planning: tool call requested turn=1 tools=1' at 23:33:32; session status tool_exec for 9+ minutes with zero tool_requests rows (executor poll log empty for that window); staging_buffer rows 1-2 carry the payloads.

findings.claim: subprocess tools silently ignore agent parameters: executeSubprocessTool runs the fixed handler_ref argv with empty stdin; agent JSON parameters are never passed (executeHTTPEndpoint is the only parameter-carrying handler: {param} URL substitution + JSON body). A tool row registered as subprocess returns garbage for parameterized calls (probe row 1 output shows the empty-stdin error).
findings.evidence: internal/harness/tool_executor.go executeSubprocessTool — executable/args come only from splitToolCommand(handlerRef); tool_results id=1 vs id=2/3.
